baseline.measurement: megakernel profiler, 48M slots, 9.3-24.7M events/run, 3 reps per batch size; profiled vs unprofiled wave wall 2.85-3.59% apart; token ids byte-identical to the committed M2 report for all 25 (prompt,bs) cases

delta_model.note: expected_e2e_delta_per_bs is step_us/(step_us - recovered_wall_us) - 1 on the STEADY DECODE STEP, i.e. AC-4 decode throughput, unless the entry says wave-level. The wall-span decomposition is near-additive: the sum of per-task-type wall spans is 109-114% of the measured step at every batch size, so removing a stage's wall span is a defensible first-order model of the step it saves. Every number here is a HYPOTHESIS to be settled by the entry's verify_cmd, never acceptance (M3 milestone rules).

levers.evidence: 3840 tasks per step at EVERY batch size (grid_dim=(mbt,1,1), 96 per layer) -- the count is set by max_num_batched_tokens=16, not by live tokens, so total worker time is flat at 84.1/82.4/76.1 ms for bs1/4/16. Its wall footprint is the single largest of any task type at bs<=4: 4540 us of the 15264 us bs1 step (29.7%), 4244 us of the bs16 step (19.3%). Mean concurrency while it runs is only 33-35 of 128 blocks, and each task takes 19.8-21.9 us to block-quantize <=8 KB of activations -- three orders of magnitude off any bandwidth bound, i.e. pure launch/latency cost. Source: pertask_by_bs.csv rows TASK_QUANTIZE_FP8_SM100, tables/bs*_concurrency.json.
levers.mechanism: A separate task per (row, tensor) for a trivially cheap elementwise+reduction op. The producer (RMS-norm, SiLU-mul) already has the values in registers; quantizing in its epilogue removes both the task and the round trip through global memory.
levers.delta_basis: lower bound = half its wall span recovered, upper bound = all of it

levers.lever: Right-size MoE expert activation to the live token count
levers.evidence: The MoE GEMM grid is grid_x = min(num_experts, mbt*topk) = min(256,128) = 128 groups x moe_n_splits=2, fixed by mbt=16 -- independent of how many tokens are really in the step (builder.py:538). Measured live (>1 us) w13 tasks per layer: 112.7 at bs1, 118.8 at bs2, 120.4 at bs4, 140.2 at bs8, 173.3 at bs16 (of 256 launched), i.e. 56.4 / 59.4 / 60.2 / 70.1 / 86.7 active expert groups of 128. Top-8 routing on ONE token needs 8. So bs1 activates ~7x more experts -- and reads ~7x more expert weight -- than the routing requires; bs4 ~1.9x; bs16 is already right-sized. MoE w13+w2 wall span is 4786 us of the bs1 step (31%). Source: pertask_by_bs.csv nlong_bs* + wallspan_us_bs*.
levers.mechanism: The router (topk_softmax_sm100) routes all mbt=16 rows including the 15 phantom rows of a 1-token decode step; each phantom row contributes its own top-8 entries to moe_routing_indices/moe_mask, so the grouped GEMM streams those experts' weights for output that is then discarded.
levers.delta_basis: MoE wall span scaled by (1 - min(128, 8*bs)/measured_active_groups)
levers.risk: medium - touches the router. Phantom-row outputs are discarded, so this should be AC-3 neutral by construction, but it must be proven per-case, and MOE_ROUTER_MAX_ROWS_PER_TASK/the 16-row cap interact (M2-I9).

levers.lever: Widen the narrow task stages (graph width, not scheduler speed)
levers.evidence: worker-idle-while-others-work is 9.57/9.44/8.76/9.92/9.91 ms per step at bs 1/2/4/8/16 -- essentially BATCH-INDEPENDENT and 45-63% of every step. Mean concurrency is 43.5/46.5/51.9/55.2/68.3 of 128 blocks; 6.7-9.1 ms of every step runs at <=16 concurrent workers. It is not a dispatch-rate or stall problem: total all-idle (nobody in a task) is only 0.50 ms/step at every bs, workers take 332-475 inter-task gaps per step of mean 21-30 us and max 164 us. The low-concurrency stages are exactly the low-task-count ones: TASK_ATTN_SM100 2/layer -> concurrency 2.0 at bs1, TASK_GDN_CONV1D 8/layer -> 8.0, TASK_RMS_NORM/SIGMOID_GATE/MOE_MUL_SUM_ADD 16/layer -> 15-16, TASK_QUANTIZE_FP8 96/layer -> 34.6. Source: attribution.csv worker_idle_us + us_at_conc_le16, tables/bs*_concurrency.json per_task_concurrency.
levers.mechanism: MPK executes one CTA per task. A stage emitting 16 tasks occupies 16 of 148 SMs for its whole duration no matter how cheap it is, and the 40 layers are strictly sequential, so those stages stack up into a batch-independent floor.
levers.delta_basis: half of the <=16-concurrency wall recovered; the perfect-packing bound (task_sum/128) says the ceiling is 2.9x at bs1 and 1.9x at bs16

levers.disposition: blocked-with-reason: Graph width is still the largest structural residual and M3 only chipped at it: I3 split GDN into separate tasks, I8 gated MoE pad rows, I6a removed the register spill that was throttling every task. What remains is a per-stage task-splitting programme -- I3 alone took a full ferret campaign plus an integration issue for ONE stage -- and it does not fit in M3's remaining budget. It is not rejected: the re-derived table shows MPK still 2.2-2.8x off vLLM overall while being AHEAD on every fused stage, which is the signature of a width problem, not a kernel-quality problem. Carried to M4 with the split-KV attention lever (M3-I6a) as the first concrete instance. Evidence opt/m3i7/stage/, opt/m3i3/, opt/m3i6a/.  || M4-I5 (2026-07-29) TERMINAL: quantified and measured. Per-stage width table at integrated HEAD (opt/m4i5/tables/width_bs*.json): at bs1 80.6% of the 9822.8us step has exactly ONE stage running and 79% runs on <=16 of 128 workers; 6580us is idle machine attributable to a single narrow stage. Largest merge-free residual is the routed MoE pair (3040us at bs1); it was PROTOTYPED behind MPK_MOE_N_SPLITS (default-off) and measures +11.1/+8.8/+7.4/+3.5% at bs1/2/4/8 and -1.0% at bs16 with k=4, against a model that predicted +34% at bs1. k=8 REJECTED (worse than k=4 at bs>=4, worse than base at bs>=8). Mechanism for the shortfall, measured on profiled arms: the split recovers width exactly (26->104 live tasks/level of 128) but is NOT work-conserving (+32%/+54% total worker time) and a dependency level has an arrival-spread floor of ~33us that the split cannot cross. CONCLUSION: width is real but is NOT the AC-4 residual -- the compiled graph's CRITICAL PATH is 4.55/5.39/6.09ms at bs1/8/16, 46-50% of the step and 1.14-1.30x vLLM's ENTIRE step, so at infinite width MPK is still slower than vLLM at every batch size. Evidence opt/m4i5/. || M4-I7 (2026-07-30) PARTIAL CLOSURE for the two MoE grouped-GEMM stages: the mechanism named here -- 'a stage emitting 16 tasks occupies 16 of 148 SMs' -- was attacked from INSIDE the kernel rather than by widening the grid. task_register.cc already emits expert_stride = grid.x = 128 tasks per (layer, stage, N-split); the golden body gave each task one expert, so with MOE_GATE_PADDING_ROWS right-sizing activation to live rows (M3-I8) only num_activated=8 of 128 were live at bs1. The ferret v012 port walks a FLATTENED (expert, N-block) work space, so the same work lands on num_activated*NUM_N_BLOCKS of the already-emitted tasks at zero extra dispatch cost and with TILE_N unchanged. Measured: w13 stage wallspan 2340.7 -> 673.1 us (3.478x) and w2 1306.2 -> 397.7 us (3.285x) at bs1, with stage WORK flat (w13 x0.994), i.e. pure packing -- pinning the golden 16 B cp.async fetch path (MPK_MOE_PATH_POLICY=0) still gives 826.2 ms vs the shipped 824.3, so the fetch path is worth 0.3% and the flattening the other 32.6%. e2e 1.3291/1.2702/1.1890/1.1541/1.1298x at bs 1/2/4/8/16, AC-3 STABLE and bit-exact 10/10 per bs, ptxas 238 -> 236 registers with no spill. RESIDUAL: at bs1 these stages are now 11.1% (w13) and 6.5% (w2) of the step and over HALF of w13's remaining wallspan is width residual (351.9 us = 52.3%), i.e. M4-I5's ~33 us/level arrival spread that no inner-loop work touches -- low-bs kernel work on these two is close to exhausted. bs16 keeps 39-40% width residual AND a live kernel margin (PATH 1 beats PATH 0 by 2.34% there). MPK_MOE_N_SPLITS is now a WORSE lever than before, not a better one: flattening already recruits the tasks it would have created without its dead-dispatch cost, so M4-I5's x1.11 must not be re-litigated on top of this. GENERALISES: any MPK task whose grid is sized by a worst-case activation count and whose body walks a serial inner dimension is leaving emitted tasks dead -- a cheap, bit-exact lever worth auditing the other grouped/routed tasks for. Evidence opt/m4i7/, integrated at 36504aa8.

levers.lever: Fix the mbt=16 admission policy: bs16 never reaches a decode steady state
levers.evidence: An exact replay of prepare_next_batch (opt/schedule_sim.py, validated against the trace's own BEGIN_TASK_GRAPH count at all five batch sizes: 109/109/109/111/203 predicted == observed) shows the bs16 wave spends 108 of 203 iterations in a MIXED prefill+decode regime and the other 95 draining, with ZERO iterations where all 16 requests decode. The first request retires at iteration 101 while another is still prefilling. Wave time splits 2754 ms mixed + 1920 ms drain of a 4695 ms wave. Cause: step 3 fills the 16-token budget greedily in slot order, so once the early slots are decoding they consume the whole budget and the late slots prefill one token at a time. Source: attribution.csv mixed_phase_*/drain_phase_*, tables/bs16_iters.csv.
levers.mechanism: max_num_batched_tokens=16 (capped by the MoE router 16-row limit, M2-I9) equals the batch size at bs16, so decode alone saturates admission and prefill starves. M3-I5b removed the router cap (row-tile loop in topk_softmax_sm100 + topk_sigmoid_sm100; shipped instantiations SASS-identical), so mbt is now a free knob -- the remaining question is profitability, not feasibility.
levers.delta_basis: idealised schedule = 36 prefill iterations at the measured 25.5 ms mixed-iteration cost + 107 decode iterations at the measured 22.0 ms
levers.risk: medium-high - changes admission and therefore AC-5 e2e and the GDN slot-compaction hazard surface (HAZARD-COMPACTION).

M3-I4's ferret loop was still climbing at min_ratio 0.680 when the box's Claude weekly quota ran out (reset 2026-07-29), and no in-MPK change landed, so there is nothing to integrate and nothing to reject. Unblocked by the quota reset; carried to M4 with the loop's current best ratio as its starting point. Evidence opt/m3i4/, the ferret episode ledger at 5cedb43c.  || M4-I2 (2026-07-29) TERMINAL: INTEGRATED. The ferret loop finished at workspace4 tag v011 (min_ratio 1.011 over 30 shape/M configs vs vLLM's cutlass_3x_gemm_fp8_blockwise; worst outproj_M2 101.1%, best gdnz_M4 128.1%) and this issue ported it into task 279. The pre-existing kernel is preserved BYTE-FOR-BYTE as linear_fp8_blockscale_task_impl_golden and the entry point is now a compile-time dispatcher; the port is bit-exact against it -- 30/30 shape/bs cases in both nvcc flag lanes AND both a torch-free 12.8 build (the shipped JIT toolchain) and the 13.0 pybind harness, with ZERO differing elements even on deliberately-inexact data. AC-3 STABLE at all five bs, 15/15 cold reps accepted, 0 quarantined, byte-identical to results/dumps_final; tokens_sha256 also matched between arms in all 15 e2e (bs,rep) pairs. ptxas unchanged vs pre-M4-I2 HEAD: 238 registers, 144 B stack, 0 spill st/ld -- so the M3-I6a class of cross-stage regression does not apply. e2e (3 reps/arm/bs, interleaved in one GPU claim, HEAD control within 0.01% of the baseline arm): +10.0/+10.0/+8.5/+7.2/+8.2% at bs 1/2/4/8/16. THE STRUCTURAL CHANGE was a per-task N slice FINER than the checkpoint's 128-row scale block (16/32/64 per shape); MPK splits inputs by integer division, so the weight scale is attached row-replicated to one row per task and linear_fp8_blockscale_layer now asserts that, closing a silent-wrong-scale hole for every caller. WHAT THIS CLOSES AND WHAT IT HANDS ON: stage wallspan 2813.8->1483.7us at bs1 (1.896x) and 2851.1->1579.6us at bs16 (1.805x), which against M3-I7's 2.07x stage deficit puts dense fp8 at roughly PARITY with vLLM -- the gap this rank tracked is gone. The win is WIDTH, not less work: aggregate per-task work ROSE 1.24x (the slice multiplies the task count ~3.2x and each task re-pays a fixed prologue) while mean concurrency during the stage went 70.8->113.0 at bs1 and 39.0->94.7 at bs16 of 128. Residual: the stage is now only 17.1% of the step at bs1 and 14.1% at bs16, so driving task 279 to ZERO would leave 7171.8 of 8655.5us and 9658.3 of 11237.9us standing -- FURTHER KERNEL WORK ON 279 IS EXHAUSTED AS A LEVER. About half of what the stage still costs is width (660.5us = 44.5% at bs1, 837.3us = 53.0% at bs16), and the largest width deficit now visible in the same profile is TASK_MOE_W13_FP8_BLOCKSCALE_SM100 (span 2343.8us at mean concurrency 95.8) -- rank 3 / M4-I5's territory, and consistent with M4-I5's finding that the compiled graph's CRITICAL PATH, not width, is the AC-4 residual. NOT DONE HERE: prefill keeps the golden path (max_num_batched_tokens > 16 falls back to slice 128, because the fast path's per-warp B ring assumes TILE_M == 16); a prefill-capable fast path needs the ring generalised to WARPS_M > 1. Evidence opt/m4i2/.

levers.disposition: rejected-with-evidence, RE-DERIVED by M4-I4 (2026-07-29) on a new basis. The M3 rejection said the precondition (more tokens per iteration) went the other way; that was an mbt argument made before the cap landed and before prefill was measured at the pinned geometry, so it is re-derived rather than inherited. Three findings, in the order that decides it. (1) Prefill IS still binding: after the cap it is 13.5%/19.7% of e2e at bs8/bs16 and still costs AC-5 a 1.075x/1.381x decode requirement, so the lever is not dead on relevance. (2) But WY/UT is not the shape of the remaining cost. It is a CHUNKED-MATMUL algorithm -- it wins by doing the delta rule as block-parallel matmuls over many tokens at once -- and the per-request chunk size under the landed policy is mbt/bs = 1 token at bs16, 2 at bs8. The cap REDUCED the per-request chunk to the minimum, and it did so because narrow chunks are what makes MPK fast here (the graph-width mechanism above). A chunked-matmul algorithm at chunk size 1 is the sequential recurrence plus bookkeeping: the winning direction is the opposite one, and that is now measured rather than argued. (3) Its numerics gate does not inherit. M3-I9b proved chunk boundaries bit-transparent in the CURRENT kernels (identical logit rows, bit-identical per-layer GDN conv and fp32 recurrent state at bs1/bs4 cap-vs-base, H1-H4 refuted with source citations), but that is about re-chopping the SAME per-token sequential recurrence. WY/UT is a block-parallel delta rule with a different summation order and different intermediate precision, so transparency cannot transfer; it would need its own bit-exactness gate against the HF chunk algorithm as oracle plus its own AC-3 sweep. For scale, the cap -- a one-min() change WITH a proven transparency argument -- still needed 300 cases to certify. RE-OPEN ONLY IF mbt RISES (the budget, not its division): larger chunks are the only thing that restores the precondition, so WY/UT must be sequenced strictly after an mbt-for-prefill landing, never before, and must carry its own oracle gate. Evidence: opt/m4i4/README.md sections 2d, 3 and 5; opt/m3i9b/ (transparency of the current kernels); opt/m3i5b/ (the mbt rejection, decode-side).
